problem:
Find the minimum value of the function
\[f(x) = \sqrt{-x^2 + 4x + 21} - \sqrt{-x^2 + 3x + 10}.\]
solution:
We can write the function as
\[f(x) = \sqrt{(7 - x)(3 + x)} - \sqrt{(5 - x)(2 + x)}.\]This shows that the function is defined only for $-2 \le x \le 5.$  Also, $(7 - x)(3 + x) - (5 - x)(2 + x) = x + 11 > 0$ on this interval, which means that $f(x)$ is always positive.

Then
\begin{align*}
[f(x)]^2 &= (7 - x)(3 + x) - 2 \sqrt{(7 - x)(3 + x)} \sqrt{(5 - x)(2 + x)} + (5 - x)(2 + x) \\
&= -2x^2 + 7x + 31 - 2 \sqrt{(7 - x)(2 + x)(5 - x)(3 + x)} \\
&= 2 + (7 - x)(2 + x) - 2 \sqrt{(7 - x)(2 + x)} \sqrt{(5 - x)(3 + x)} + (5 - x)(3 + x) \\
&= 2 + \left[ \sqrt{(7 - x)(2 + x)} - \sqrt{(5 - x)(3 + x)} \right]^2 \ge 2.
\end{align*}Therefore, $f(x) \ge \sqrt{2}.$

Equality occurs when $(7 - x)(2 + x) = (5 - x)(3 + x),$ or $x = \frac{1}{3}.$  We conclude that the minimum value is $\boxed{\sqrt{2}}.$

\end{align*}By QM-AM,

\[\sqrt{(7 - x)(x + 3)} + \sqrt{(5 - x)(x + 2)} \le \sqrt{2[(7 - x)(x + 3) + (5 - x)(x + 2)]} = \sqrt{-4x^2 + 28x + 82}.\]Hence,
\[f(x) \ge \sqrt{(7 - x)(x + 3)} - \sqrt{-4x^2 + 28x + 82}.\]Again by QM-AM,
\[\sqrt{\frac{(7 - x)(x + 3) + (-4x^2 + 28x + 82)}{2}} \ge \frac{\sqrt{(7 - x)(x + 3)} + \sqrt{-4x^2 + 28x + 82}}{2}.\]Then
\[\sqrt{(7 - x)(x + 3)} + \sqrt{-4x^2 + 28x + 82} \le \sqrt{2[(7 - x)(x + 3) + (-4x^2 + 28x + 82)]} = \sqrt{-10x^2 + 60x + 290}.\]Hence,
\[f(x) \ge -\sqrt{-10x^2 + 60x + 290}.\]Completing the square in $x,$ we get
\[-\sqrt{-10x^2 + 60x + 290} = -\sqrt{-(10x^2 - 60x - 290)} = -\sqrt{-10(x - 3)^2 + 380}.\]The maximum value of this expression occurs when $x = 3,$ so the minimum value is $-\sqrt{380} = \boxed{-2 \sqrt{95}}.$

Equality occurs when $\sqrt{(7 - x)(x + 3)} = \sqrt{-4x^2 + 28x + 82}$ and $\sqrt{(7 - x)(x + 3)} = -2 \sqrt{-x^2 + 3x + 10},$ or $x = 3,$ so the minimum value is indeed $-2 \sqrt{95}.$
